concept.title: Pseudo-classes
concept.shortdesc: A pseudo-class starts with : and tests something about an element, such as its position in the XML tree, its language, or an interaction state. Some pseudo-classes can be evaluated from the XML tree. Others depend on interaction states, a media timeline, or meanings defined by a document vocabulary, which CSSMedia does not use when processing a PDF.

conbody.p: CSSMedia accepts selector syntax only when it recognizes that syntax. A recognized pseudo-class does not necessarily match an element. The guides below distinguish pseudo-classes CSSMedia can use to match XML elements from valid pseudo-classes it accepts but does not match in PDF processing.

section.title: Child and sibling position
section.p: “Selectors 4 §13, Tree-Structural pseudo-classes”.
Structural pseudo-classes select elements by their position among siblings in the XML tree. They do not depend on how the elements are displayed.

:first-child, :last-child and :only-child count all element siblings. The -of-type forms count siblings with the same element name and namespace. Text, comments and processing instructions are not counted as element siblings.

section.title: Nth-position selectors
section.p: “Selectors 4 §13.3, Child-indexed Pseudo-classes”.
Use an :nth-* pseudo-class to select an element by its numbered position among siblings. Positions start at one. odd and even select alternating positions; An+B describes a repeating sequence.

The of clause in :nth-child() and :nth-last-child() filters the siblings before CSSMedia counts them. The -last- forms count from the end. The -of-type forms count only siblings with the same element name and namespace.
CSSMedia matches :nth-child(), :nth-last-child(), :nth-of-type() and :nth-last-of-type().

section.title: Column position
section.p: “Selectors 5 §8.2, :nth-col() pseudo-class”; “Selectors 5 §8.3, :nth-last-col() pseudo-class”.
:nth-col() and :nth-last-col() select cells by their position in a table column.

section.title: Root, empty and scope
section.p: “Selectors 4 §13.1, :root pseudo-class”; “Selectors 4 §13.2, :empty pseudo-class”; “Selectors 4 §8.4, The Reference Element Pseudo-class: :scope”.

:root selects the root element of the XML document. :empty selects an element with no child elements or non-whitespace text. Whitespace-only text, comments and processing instructions do not prevent an element from matching :empty.
:scope selects the current scoping element. When CSSMedia matches a selector without another scope, the document root is the scope.
CSSMedia matches these pseudo-classes using the XML tree. The nesting selector & is different from a pseudo-class. It refers to the parent selector inside a nested rule.

section.title: Selector-list and relational pseudo-classes
section.p: “Selectors 4 §4.2, The Matches-Any Pseudo-class: :is()”; “Selectors 4 §4.3, The Negation (Matches-None) Pseudo-class: :not()”; “Selectors 4 §4.4, The Specificity-adjustment Pseudo-class: :where()”; “Selectors 4 §4.5, The Relational Pseudo-class: :has()”.

These pseudo-classes let you combine selectors. :is() matches an element if it matches at least one selector in its argument. :where() works the same way but adds no specificity. :not() excludes elements that match its argument. :has() selects an element based on a related element.

:not() makes the selector invalid if its argument contains an invalid selector. :is() and :where() discard invalid selectors from their lists. CSSMedia also accepts :matches() as an alias for :is(). A :has() argument cannot contain another :has() or a pseudo-element.

section.title: Language and direction
section.p: “Selectors 4 §7.1, The Directionality Pseudo-class: :dir()”; “Selectors 4 §7.2, The Language Pseudo-class: :lang()”.
Use :lang() to select elements by language. CSSMedia checks the nearest xml:lang value on the element or its ancestors.

If no language is set, :lang("") matches. For :dir(ltr) and :dir(rtl), CSSMedia scans the element’s descendant text for the first strong character using the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm. If there is none, it checks the nearest inherited, normalized xml:lang value and uses its bidi classification. If there is no language or it is not classified as bidi, the direction defaults to left-to-right. The CSS direction property does not affect :dir().

section.title: Links and document location
section.p: “Selectors 4 §8.1, The Hyperlink Pseudo-class: :any-link”; “Selectors 4 §8.2, The Link History Pseudo-classes: :link and :visited”; “Selectors 4 §8.3, The Target Pseudo-class: :target”; “Selectors 5 §2.1, The Local Link Pseudo-class :local-link”.

CSSMedia uses its link property to identify elements with hyperlink destinations. :link and :any-link select those elements. :local-link selects a link to the same document. Its optional integer limits the number of path segments compared.

CSSMedia does not track browsing history, so it does not distinguish visited links. :visited and :target are accepted but do not match elements. The link property is a CSSMedia extension; it supplies link destinations for XML elements.

section.title: User interaction
section.p: “Selectors 4 §9, User Action Pseudo-classes”; “Selectors 5 §3.1, The Interest Pseudo-classes: :interest-source and :interest-target”.

User-action pseudo-classes describe states such as pointing at an element, activating it, or giving it keyboard focus. Interest pseudo-classes describe a user indicating interest in an element. These states require interaction; they do not occur during PDF processing.

:hover means a pointing device is over an element. :active means the element is being activated. :focus means it has input focus; :focus-visible means that focus should be indicated; and :focus-within also matches an element containing the focused element. :interest-source and :interest-target identify the source and target of a user’s declared interest.
CSSMedia accepts these selectors, but none match elements in PDF processing.

section.title: Media playback and time
section.p: “Selectors 4 §10.1, Media Playback State: the :playing, :paused, and :seeking pseudo-classes”; “Selectors 4 §10.2, Media Loading State: the :buffering and :stalled pseudo-classes”; “Selectors 4 §10.3, Sound State: the :muted and :volume-locked pseudo-classes”; “Selectors 5 §5.1, The Current-element Pseudo-class: :current”; “Selectors 5 §5.2, The Past-element Pseudo-class: :past”; “Selectors 5 §5.3, The Future-element Pseudo-class: :future”.

:playing, :paused and :seeking describe playback state. :buffering and :stalled describe media loading. :muted and :volume-locked describe sound state. The time-dimensional pseudo-classes :current, :current(...), :past and :future describe elements in relation to a timeline, such as the current playback position or speech rendering.
CSSMedia accepts these pseudo-classes, but none match elements in a PDF. CSSMedia has no media playback state or timeline to evaluate.

section.title: Input and interface state
section.p: “Selectors 4 §12.1.1, The :enabled and :disabled Pseudo-classes”; “Selectors 4 §12.1.2, The Mutability Pseudo-classes: :read-only and :read-write”; “Selectors 4 §12.1.3, The Placeholder-shown Pseudo-class: :placeholder-shown”; “Selectors 4 §12.1.4, The Automatic Input Pseudo-class: :autofill”; “Selectors 4 §12.1.5, The Default-option Pseudo-class: :default”; “Selectors 4 §12.2.1, The Selected-option Pseudo-classes: :checked, :unchecked, and :indeterminate”; “Selectors 4 §12.3.1, The Validity Pseudo-classes: :valid and :invalid”; “Selectors 4 §12.3.2, The Range Pseudo-classes: :in-range and :out-of-range”; “Selectors 4 §12.3.3, The Optionality Pseudo-classes: :required and :optional”; “Selectors 4 §12.3.4, The User-interaction Pseudo-classes: :user-valid and :user-invalid”; “Selectors 5 §4.1.1, The Empty-Value Pseudo-class: :blank”.

These pseudo-classes describe form controls and interface states. :enabled and :disabled test whether a control can be used. :read-write tests whether its value can be changed; :placeholder-shown tests whether placeholder text is visible; :autofill tests whether a value was filled automatically; and :default identifies a default control. :checked, :unchecked and :indeterminate test selection state. :valid and :invalid test constraint validation; :in-range and :out-of-range test a value against its allowed range. :required and :optional test whether a value is required. :user-valid and :user-invalid test validity after user interaction. :blank tests whether a control’s value is empty.
Their meaning depends on behavior defined by a host language, such as HTML. CSSMedia treats XML names and attributes as data and does not infer that an element is a form control.

CSSMedia accepts :enabled, :disabled, :read-write, :placeholder-shown, :autofill, :default, :checked, :unchecked, :indeterminate, :blank, :valid, :invalid, :in-range, :out-of-range, :required, :optional, :user-valid and :user-invalid, but none match elements. :read-only matches every element.

section.title: Document-language-defined states
section.p: “Selectors 5 §6, Exposing custom state: the :state() pseudo-class”; “Selectors 5 §7, Heading Structures: the heading pseudo-classes :heading, and :heading()”.

Some pseudo-classes depend on states or semantics supplied by a document vocabulary. :state(name) checks a custom element state. :heading and :heading() depend on which elements the vocabulary defines as headings and what levels they represent.
CSSMedia accepts :state(), :heading and :heading(), but they do not match elements because CSSMedia does not assign custom states or heading semantics to XML elements.

section.title: Interface and presentation states
section.p: “Selectors 4 §11.1, Collapse State: the :open pseudo-class”; “Selectors 4 §11.2, Popover State: the :popover-open pseudo-class”; “Selectors 4 §11.3, Modal (Exclusive Interaction) State: the :modal pseudo-class”; “Selectors 4 §11.4, Fullscreen Presentation State: the :fullscreen pseudo-class”; “Selectors 4 §11.5, Picture-in-Picture Presentation State: the :picture-in-picture pseudo-class”.

:open identifies an open or expanded element. :popover-open identifies an open popover. :modal identifies an element in modal presentation. :fullscreen identifies an element shown in fullscreen mode, and :picture-in-picture identifies an element presented in picture-in-picture mode.
These are interface or presentation states that CSSMedia does not provide. It accepts the pseudo-classes, but they do not match elements.

section.title: Defined elements
section.p: “Selectors 4 §5.4, The Defined Pseudo-class: :defined”.

:defined tests whether the document vocabulary distinguishes fully defined elements from undefined ones. XML as processed by CSSMedia has no separate defined or constructed state, so :defined matches every element.
